subject: business-studies
title: Profitability Ratios
welcome_lead: Gross margin, net margin and ROCE - three lenses on profitability.
meta_desc: A-Level Ratio Analysis: gross margin, net margin and ROCE.
final_note: ROCE links profit to the capital actually invested - it is the investor's favourite.

concepts.def: Gross profit divided by revenue, times 100.
Operating profit divided by revenue, times 100.
Net profit divided by revenue, times 100.
Operating profit divided by capital employed, times 100.
Comparing ratios with rivals or industry averages.

walkthroughs.body_html: Gross margin covers cost of sales; operating margin deducts overheads; net margin deducts interest and tax. Gap between gross and net shows overhead and finance burden.
ROCE = (operating profit / capital employed) x 100. Capital employed = equity + long-term liabilities. ROCE of 15 to 25 percent is strong; under 5 percent worries investors.
Net margin can flatter a firm that has shrunk; ROCE penalises bloated balance sheets. Investors compare ROCE to the cost of capital - if ROCE exceeds the cost, value is being created.
